correctness.rationale: For nonzero a,b with c=ab in F_p^×, character column t↦ω(t)^r transforms the cross-hyperbola Fourier matrix into the inverse-character column times K_r=Σ_{u≠0}ω(u)^r ζ_p^{u+c/u}; since p−1 is invertible in R=Z_p[ζ_p], this gives an integral invertible diagonalization up to permutation. Writing π=ζ_p−1, the j-th binomial coefficient reduces mod p to Σ_u u^r binom(u+c/u,j). Multiplicative power-sum orthogonality forces vanishing for j<d_r=min(r,p−1−r) and yields a unit first coefficient at j=d_r for every r except the quadratic r=(p−1)/2 under nonsquare c. For that mode, the involution u↔c/u pairs terms with opposite quadratic-character weights and cancels K_m identically, not merely to finite valuation. The valuations are 0,1,1,...,m−1,m−1,m for square c and replace m with an infinite valuation for nonsquare c, including p=3. The determinant/nonzero-product valuations and complex rank follow. Independently computed all predicted initial binomial character coefficients for both square classes at p=3,5,7,11,13; checked the exact center-mode cancellation. Arithmetic calculations are finite supporting checks, while the orthogonality/π-adic argument holds for every odd prime.
